estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Textual embedding analysis of similarity among the flash-fiction outputs. The PDF does not identify the embedding model, exact similarity metric, comparison pool, or aggregation procedure (PDF p. 21, Supplementary Analysis).

sources.locator: PDF p. 21, Experiment 1, Supplementary Analysis, second analysis
sources.quote: Interestingly, our findings showed no significant increase in similarity among AI-assisted outputs compared to those created independently, indicating that AI use in our study did not homogenize creative work.

estimates.notes: Qualitative full-sample arm comparison retained under the codebook rule for contrasts without a printed number. This is not a zero effect: the paper supplies no arm levels, difference, coefficient, test statistic, standard error, confidence interval, or exact p-value. The similarity analysis does not print its own participant count or observation unit, so the study-level count is not copied into n_total. Each participant was assigned a flash-fiction task (PDF p. 16); the screening form retains this outcome as across_people. The regression specification for the supplementary similarity analysis is not described. Online Appendix D is cited for further supplementary details (PDF p. 22) but was unavailable. The sources fields list is empty because no numerical result is recorded.

not_extracted.what: S2-O7: Similarity of lyrics, both embedding cosine-similarity and L2-distance variants; AI-assisted group versus Control (no AI)
not_extracted.reason: The main text reports coefficients and p-values (PDF pp. 28-29) but never defines which outputs are compared. The analyzed sample includes multiple works by some participants (PDF p. 24). As flagged in the reconciled screening form, the available evidence cannot establish whether this measures diversity across different people or variation within a person. Its question and construct therefore cannot be confirmed under extraction-spec rule 4 and codebook section 6. The supplementary regression specification, including any post-treatment adjustment, is also unreported. The linked materials were inaccessible; the result is left pending rather than assigned an invented across_people classification.

open_items: Unadjusted arm means and participant-level SDs, or full-sample treatment effects that omit post-treatment controls, are not printed for the human-rated outcomes. The AI-identification controls are verified on PDF pp. 17, 19, 26, 41, and 43-47. These outcomes require eligible results before quantitative extraction.

For S1 story similarity, obtain both arm levels, the exact metric and embedding model, the comparison and aggregation procedure, analysis counts, and the paper’s uncertainty. None is printed in the supplementary similarity paragraph (PDF p. 21); the regression specification is also not given.

For S2 lyric similarity, establish whether comparisons are between different people and how multiple works from the same person are handled before classifying the outcome. Also obtain arm levels, embedding model, analysis unit and counts, regression controls, and uncertainty (PDF pp. 24, 28-29).

Exact numbers randomized and per-arm analyzed counts are not explicitly printed for either study. S2 reports Nstart = 685 and Ninformation = 611 (PDF p. 23), then Nsubmission = 348 and the selected analysis sample (PDF p. 24); these stages do not unambiguously give a randomized total. AI-interaction subgroup counts (PDF pp. 21, 28) are not confirmed full-arm counts and were not added to infer them.

S2 regression tables analyze 329 works (PDF pp. 43-47), whereas PDF p. 24 explicitly reports 299 participants. The tables label SEs robust but do not state participant clustering; future eligible outcome analyses must account for repeated outputs from some people.

Online Appendices A-F and linked data, code, and output remain unverified. On 2026-10-10, Python urllib requests with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/ynhtu/files/?view_only=31642f7caac74082940eb1153d4e9e55 and then the printed alternative https://osf.io/ynhtu/?view_only=31642f7caac74082940eb1153d4e9e55 both failed with WinError 10013 (socket access forbidden). No supplementary content was inferred from the failed requests.
S2 recruitment country is not explicitly stated (PDF pp. 22-24), so country is null. GPT-4 is named (PDF p. 16), but its release year is not printed, so ai_tool.year is null in both studies.
Participant overlap between experiments or with other papers is not stated. The broader-project footnote on PDF p. 16 does not establish shared participants; shared_sample is null in both studies.
notes: Extraction A, 2026-10-10. Read the entire saved markdown in contiguous chunks through its end, including references, tables, and figure captions; the referenced online appendices are absent. Extracted and checked the text of every cited PDF page with pymupdf. PDF page indices plus one match the printed page numbers. The saved PDF hash matches the citation record. Both experiments satisfy the study-level random-assignment and analyzed-people criteria, but the reported rated-output treatment effects are excluded by the post-treatment-adjustment rule. The sole estimate record is the qualitative S1 similarity contrast; all its numeric statistics and analysis counts are null. No effect, variance, arm count, or missing p-value was calculated or inferred. Participant counts are kept separate from works and raters. The exclusion log includes each screened rated outcome, the unresolved S2 similarity outcome, self-reports, moderation analyses, and AI-interaction process outcomes. The OSF access failures and missing information are documented in open_items.
